observations: Photo 0: a long automatic gearbox with a bolted-on transfer case at the rear, still mated to a V6 petrol engine, lying on a wet yard floor among other used engines and gearboxes.

Photo 0: a white sticker label on the transfer case area is visible but unreadable at this resolution; hand-written chalk marks 'CA' and a scrawl on the casing; overlaid watermark 'POSTED ON JIJI GEARUP INC'.
Photo 0 and photo 2: transfer case output flanges are rusty, a loose rusted bracket hangs off the side, transmission cooler lines and wiring harness still attached.

Photo 1: the same gearbox and transfer case seen from the other end, coupled to a V6 engine with a black plastic upper intake and a yellow dipstick handle; a person in boots stands among stacked used engines.
Photo 2: closer view of the same unit; casing is dusty and oily but no visible cracks or broken mounting ears.
No photo shows a readable tag, part number, VIN plate or brand on the gearbox or transfer case.
No photo shows the unit running, shifting, fluid condition or the inside of the pan.
The unit is sold as removed, mated to an engine, so it is unclear whether the gearbox alone or the engine plus gearbox is offered.

read_from: photo 0 shape only: automatic gearbox with transfer case, no readable tag

claims.claim: Gearbox / transmission for Jeep Wrangler 3.6L 2011 to 2017 4x4
claims.evidence: No tag, part number or VIN is readable in any photo. The engine in photo 1 is a V6 consistent with a 3.6, but fitment cannot be read off the item.
Origin cannot be shown by photos; the listing names both America and Belgium.
No clip of the unit running or shifting; priced as not working.
A removed gearbox carries no odometer; no donor vehicle mileage or record shown.
No close-up of bolt heads, pan gasket and seals to show they are undisturbed.

risks.risk: The gearbox is not the Jeep Wrangler 3.6 unit claimed; fitment and model set the price and are not readable.
risks.proof: Sharp close-up of the gearbox ID tag or stamped part number and the transfer case tag, readable, with a handwritten code and date in shot.
risks.if_unproven: cannot be priced as a Wrangler gearbox; held until the tag is readable

risks.risk: Internal wear or failure (slipping, harsh shifts, burnt clutches) despite 'tested and working'.
risks.proof: Clip of the unit installed or on a test rig running through all gears including reverse and 4x4 engagement, with the code in shot.
risks.if_unproven: as not working, core value only

risks.risk: Transfer case damage or missing internals; the 4x4 function is unproven.
risks.proof: Clip of the transfer case shifting between 2H, 4H and 4L with output shafts turning.
risks.if_unproven: transfer case priced as scrap core

risks.risk: Burnt or contaminated fluid, metal in the pan, or a previously opened unit.
risks.proof: Photo of fluid drained onto white cloth and the pan magnet, plus close-ups of pan bolts and seals.

risks.risk: Unclear whether the engine shown attached is part of the sale.
risks.proof: Seller statement plus a photo of the gearbox alone, separated from the engine.

proof_requests: Readable close-up of the gearbox ID tag or stamped part number, and the transfer case tag, with a handwritten code and today's date in the frame.
Clip of the unit running through all gears and 4x4 ranges, with the same code in shot.
Photo of the drained fluid and pan magnet.
Close-ups of pan bolts and seals to support 'never opened'.
Confirmation whether the attached engine is included.
response.reason: This is a used automatic gearbox with a transfer case, but the tag that sets its fitment and model cannot be read in any photo, so not even a worst case price for the claimed Jeep Wrangler 3.6 unit is possible. A readable tag or part number would allow pricing as not working until a running clip is shown.
